scope: robolab BananaThenRubiksCubeTask at the pinned revision; generated per predicate family (ordered_in_container); seed-0 witness pending. Semantic projection of the official termination, not physical qualification.
task_language: put the banana then the cube in the bowl

predicate_and_helpers.basis: Read BananaThenRubiksCubeTask terminations: success = objects_placed_in_container_in_order(objects=['banana', 'rubiks_cube'], container='bowl', tolerance=0.0, require_contact_with=True, require_gripper_detached=True), and the helpers in conditionals.py and predicate_logic.py; RobolabEnv records success as the TerminationManager's terminated flag, the OR of every non-timeout term.

reset_and_randomization.basis: Scene rubiks_cube_banana_bowl.usda: banana, rubiks_cube, bowl among 4 contact objects. The env's only event is reset_scene_to_default and the task adds none, so every seed resets to the same authored layout; a seed varies physics only.

assets_and_frames.basis: Each placement uses the object_in_container hull test in the container's frame; the latch reads env.episode_length_buf at the first true step.

success_timing.basis: DoneTerm success is evaluated every control step; RobolabEnv freezes the env at the first true step (a termination within its first two steps is reset as a physics artifact) and the ORA session latches it. Placement order is latched at each object's first placement.

public_observability.basis: At reset every named object (3) projects into the over-shoulder or wrist camera with a depth reading that does not hide it (witness sha256 609b05d9dee5).

success_witness.basis: Witness (seed 0, sha256 609b05d9dee5): in_order -> True; each case from a fresh reset, objects placed by direct state edits with the robot held.

counterexamples.basis: Witness (seed 0, sha256 609b05d9dee5): reset_state -> False; beside -> False; wrong_order -> False.

no_expert_strategy.basis: Clauses state end conditions only; no approach, grasp, route or motion advice.

privacy.basis: No coordinates, thresholds, fixture or object identifiers, joint values or predicate names enter the public text; numeric limits stay in this private record.

conditions.source_basis: success = objects_placed_in_container_in_order(objects=['banana', 'rubiks_cube'], container='bowl', tolerance=0.0, require_contact_with=True, require_gripper_detached=True): object_in_container's hull-centroid test, contact and release per object, with each object's first true step latched, plus contact with the container.
conditions.interpretation: Both in the bowl, touching it, the banana placed first.

conditions.source_basis: require_gripper_detached=True: gripper_detached checks that no gripper body touches the object above 0.1 N.
conditions.interpretation: Release: the gripper touches none of the named objects.
Hull slack, contact force bar and the placement latch withheld.

public_clauses: Both the banana and the cube must end up inside the bowl, each touching it.
The banana must come to rest in the bowl before the cube does: the order is fixed the first time each of them rests there, released, and taking one out again does not undo it.
Let go of each of them: the task is not complete while the gripper still touches either one.

counterexamples.case: Objects in place while one is still gripped: false by gripper_detached (source-derived, not executed).

termination_vs_subtasks.subtasks: pick_and_place(groups=['banana'], logical=all) score=1.0; pick_and_place(groups=['rubiks_cube'], logical=all) score=1.0
notes: relation: subtasks score ['object_in_container'], the termination checks ['objects_placed_in_container_in_order']
contact: the termination also requires contact with bowl

notes.detail: a wrong first placement can never succeed later in the episode (first placements are latched)

witness_plan.note: each case starts from a fresh reset of seed 0; the robot holds its reset pose with the gripper open unless a case grasps; success is any official result over the case's ticks

limitations: Generated from the pinned source; the witness (phase B) covers seed 0 only and uses direct state edits or scripted moves, never a policy rollout. Source-derived negative cases marked as such are not executed.
